checkpoints: After each edit burst, observe that no store write occurs before the 120 ms quiet interval and that exactly the latest text is written when the interval completes.
After a completed save, start another burst and verify it independently schedules and completes a later save.
Navigate or close before a pending save fires and verify the document buffer still saves while the retired view subscription no longer owns badge/status updates.
Exercise synchronous navigation from a save-triggered store listener and verify the resulting current view is not overwritten by stale continuation.
Verify search preview behavior remains unchanged, including its separate 40 ms trailing interval.
Run the public JavaScript/Vue syntax or build checks after any Action.
forbidden_effects: Do not write each keystroke directly to the store.
Do not save an intermediate edit from a burst when a later edit arrives within the 120 ms quiet interval.
Do not cancel or discard a document's pending buffer merely because its view is closed, replaced, or disposed.
Do not let a retired view retain its live store subscription or receive badge/status ownership.
Do not merge document-buffer timing or lifecycle with the search preview task.
Do not change public interfaces, source identity/text semantics, or status payload semantics.
Do not modify tests or configuration during an Action.
lifecycle_identity: Each document id identifies its own persistent document buffer in BufferBank.
The document buffer exists independently of the current view badge and may outlive view navigation, close, or disposal.
The current view owns the live store subscription represented by stop; replacing or closing the view retires that subscription.
Search preview owns a distinct transient trailing task and lifecycle.

obligations.text: Coalesce editor edits per document with the existing trailing-task utility using a 120 ms quiet interval.
Within an editing burst, persist only the latest supplied text after 120 ms without another edit.
After one burst saves, later bursts must remain schedulable and save normally.
Keep document buffers owned by the separate BufferBank and independent of the current view badge, so view retirement does not cancel pending document work.
Preserve open, edit, close, and dispose public interfaces and the editor's other observable behavior, including view subscription retirement and document rendering semantics.
Handle synchronous navigation caused by save callbacks without allowing stale work from an earlier navigation request to replace or corrupt the newer current view.
Leave the adjacent search preview and its distinct quiet interval unchanged.
Retain original source identities/text and status payload semantics across delayed saves.

ordering_barriers: For a burst, each new edit must replace the trailing task's pending value and restart its 120 ms timer; persistence occurs only after the final timer completes.
When a view is retired, clear the published current view and stop its live subscription before publishing a replacement view.
A delayed save's store write may synchronously notify listeners and cause navigation; any continuation belonging to an older navigation request must not overwrite the newer request's view.
Document-buffer lifecycle and cancellation must remain separate from current-view subscription lifecycle.
Search preview scheduling remains independent from document-edit scheduling.
preservation: Preserve createWorkspace behavior exposed as open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose().
Preserve current document rendering on open and null rendering on retirement.
Preserve synchronous store read/write/subscribe behavior apart from the intentionally delayed editor write.
Preserve live badge/status subscription ownership by the current view only.
Preserve pending document buffers across view changes because they persist independently of the current view badge.
Preserve all original identity, text, revision/status payload meanings.
Preserve createSearchPreview query(text), hide(), and its existing 40 ms trailing behavior.
scope: Business-code maintenance is limited to the workspace draft editor's document edit/save coordination and its use of the existing trailing utility.
Relevant public business sources are src/coordinator.js, src/services.js, src/Workspace.vue, README.md, and docs/host-api.md.
The adjacent search preview is explicitly outside the maintenance change.
Any Action may edit only business code under /workspace and must preserve tests and configuration.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));

triggers: Calling edit(text) while a document view is current starts or refreshes that document's 120 ms trailing save.
A further edit for the same document before the timer fires replaces the pending text and restarts the quiet interval.
Timer completion after 120 ms of quiet flushes the latest pending text to the store.
Opening another document, closing, or disposing retires the current view but does not retire the document buffer.
The delayed store write synchronously notifies active store listeners, which may synchronously initiate navigation.
Calling search preview query(text) continues to use its separate 40 ms task; hide() cancels that preview task.

The originals do not state whether repeated open(id) calls should reuse any view-level state beyond reusing the document buffer.
The originals do not define behavior for non-string text, null ids, invalid service objects, or edits made with no current view beyond the existing observable no-op.
The originals do not prescribe a particular internal reentrancy mechanism; only the documented synchronous-navigation behavior and preserved outcomes are normative.
